title: MicroTriager: SparkRunner compact admin toolbox for rapid triage & runbook-as-task synthesis
creator: Riya Patel
description:
Problem: On-call engineers spend 2-6 minutes rebuilding request context and choosing the right runbook variant for common incidents (cache evictions, model OOMs, routing thrash). Goal: deliver a compact, interactive admin toolkit (MicroTriager / SparkRunner) that exposes curated, typed runbooks as single-click tasklets with safe dry-run and quick-roll remediation. The feature bridges runbooks-as-tasks and support automation: synthesize a minimal sequence (1-3 steps) from existing playbooks, surface required inputs from the request context snapshot, and provide a gated execute path with telemetry and auto-rollback triggers.

Scope: MVP feature set includes: 1) a tasklet generator that converts canonical runbooks into selectable steps with typed params; 2) an in-console dry-run simulator that replays steps against a sandboxed state snapshot; 3) guarded execution with RBAC + safety veto rules; 4) telemetry hooks (token-level cost, step latency, success/failure, revert triggers) and an incident audit log; 5) QA fixtures and a small set of curated tasklets for common incidents (kv-cache-evict, model-restart, routing-fallback).

Why different: existing runbook playbook work focuses on large orchestration. MicroTriager prioritizes short, human-in-the-loop microactions for fast MTTI reduction and predictable unit-costs. The SparkRunner engine prefers idempotent, composable primitives and auto-synthesizes parameter suggestions from context snapshots (recent requests, shard ids, model version).
comments: 2025-02-21 - Riya Patel: Kickoff meeting notes posted. Agreed MVP must support dry-run vs live execute and include an RBAC gating layer. Action: engineering to prototype step templating and context snapshot API.

2025-02-25 - Evan Michaels: PoC of the step templater is functional. It converts 4 canonical runbooks into typed tasklets. Observed that parameter inference for shard IDs works ~85% on test traces; fallback to manual input required for edge cases.

2025-02-27 - Design review (Ava Morgan): UX feedback - show an explicit 'safety rating' per tasklet and require two-step confirmation for high-risk ops. Suggested inline link to the relevant incident dashboard.
2025-03-01 - Security review (Priya Singh): Requirement: all live executions must require a recent MFA token + role check. Flagged KMS usage for any secrets passed to steplets.

2025-03-03 - Evan Michaels: Integration PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4821. Tests added for dry-run simulation harness, plus telemetry spans (trace IDs emitted). Seeking review from infra owners (ENG-271555).
acceptance_criteria: Generate typed tasklet from a canonical runbook and surface inferred params in the UI
Dry-run simulator replays the tasklet against a snapshot without mutating production state
Live execute path enforces RBAC + MFA check and emits telemetry spans to tracing
Automatic revert triggers bound to a failure policy (e.g., >1 step failure triggers rollback)
Owners can add a tasklet to the curated library via a PR-like review workflow
implementation_notes: Architecture: implement a small templating layer that maps runbook steps -> action primitives. Keep runtime engine separate from admin UI; engine exposes a dry-run flag that switches to sandboxed persistence.
Context snapshots: extend existing request-trace API to return last-5 requests, model_version, shard_ids and cache keys. Snapshot size limit = 32KB per snapshot to bound storage costs.
Safety: use existing guardrail service for permission checks, and wire in the recent MFA token check. High-risk tasklets require two approvers for execution.
Telemetry: emit an event for each step with fields: trace_id, tasklet_id, step_idx, latency_ms, result, cost_units. Hook into console trace panel and incident dashboard.
Testing: build a synthetic incident harness that replays historical traces from the last 90 days for QA. Add unit tests for parameter inference edge cases.
risks: Parameter inference may suggest incorrect shard IDs in multi-tenant request traces leading to unsafe ops — mitigated by explicit confirmation and a dry-run default.
Sandboxed dry-run must be reliably isolated; any leakage to production state would be high-severity. Plan to audit sandbox boundaries as part of security review.
Overbroad curated library might lead to non-idempotent actions being exposed — require PR review and a small whitelist for MVP.
rollout_plan: Week 1: internal dogfood in Ops team with dry-run only access
Week 2: enable execute for senior oncall (canary group) with telemetry monitoring
Week 3: expand to full oncall with automatic revert policies enforced
Post-release: collect MTTI and step success metrics for 30 days and iterate
